name: Temporary mortgage buydown
title: Temporary mortgage buydown: Formula, Example & Limits
description: A temporary mortgage buydown is an arrangement that uses subsidy funds to cover part of a borrower’s scheduled early mortgage payments.
definition: A temporary mortgage buydown is an arrangement that uses subsidy funds to cover part of a borrower’s scheduled early mortgage payments. In the modeled arrangement, the mortgage note rate and full lender payment stay fixed.
explanation: A 2-1 plan uses a two-percentage-point borrower calculation reduction in year one and one point in year two. The subsidy fills the payment gap; it is distinct from paying discount points for a different permanent note rate.
formula: Subsidy = full note-rate P&I − reduced borrower P&I
formulaNote: Fixed-rate, monthly amortizing loans only. Tax, insurance, mortgage insurance and closing charges are excluded. No eligibility, approval, source-of-funds limits or unused subsidy refund is determined.

example.title: A 2-1 buydown starts a $300,000 loan at $1,610.46 a month
example.intro: $300,000 loan; 7% fixed note rate; 360 monthly payments; 2-1 temporary buydown.
steps: Calculate the lender payment at the 7% note rate over the full 360-month term.
Calculate the first-year borrower payment using 5% over that same original principal and term. The second-year borrower calculation uses 6%.
Subsidy funds cover the difference between the borrower payment and the unchanged contract payment. Taxes and insurance are outside these amounts.
example.answer: First-year borrower principal and interest is $1,610.46 per month. Budget for the payment increase when each temporary reduction ends.
example.assumptions: Fixed-rate, monthly amortizing loans only. Tax, insurance, mortgage insurance and closing charges are excluded. No eligibility, approval, source-of-funds limits or unused subsidy refund is determined.

pitfall.title: Subsidy funding is not contractual interest saved
pitfall.text: The same full loan payment is credited using borrower funds plus subsidy. The original note-rate amortization continues; evaluate who supplies the subsidy and the actual agreement separately.

tools.text: Compare the borrower payment, subsidy funding and unchanged full lender payment.
Separate the loan payment from entered taxes, insurance and broader housing costs.

name: Cash-secured put
title: Cash-secured put: Formula, Example & Limits
description: A cash-secured put is a short put backed by cash intended to fund buying the contract shares at the strike if assignment occurs.
definition: A cash-secured put is a short put backed by cash intended to fund buying the contract shares at the strike if assignment occurs. Receiving premium limits the potential gain but does not remove losses when the shares fall substantially.
explanation: For standard share delivery, the modeled secured amount is strike multiplied by covered shares before premium credit. Economic breakeven subtracts net premium per share from the strike. Broker cash treatment and early assignment need separate contract information.
formula: Expiration P&L = net premium − max(strike − stock price, 0) × shares
formulaNote: Manual, standard share-delivery puts held to expiration. No live option chain, fair-value pricing, early-close model, assignment probability or tax calculation. Broker collateral rules can differ.

example.title: At $45 per share: premium offsets part of a $1,000 obligation
example.intro: Strike $50; premium $2.50 per share; two contracts of 100 shares each; $4 total fees; assumed expiration stock price $45.00.
steps: The same trade still receives $496 net premium; do not subtract the $4 fees a second time.
Intrinsic obligation is ($50 − $45) × 200 = $1,000. Subtract it from net premium.
If the shares are delivered at the strike, $47.52 is the modeled net economic acquisition cost per share under these inputs, not a completed tax-basis record.
example.answer: Modeled expiration loss is $504. A positive premium receipt does not ensure a profitable trade.
example.assumptions: Manual, standard share-delivery puts held to expiration. No live option chain, fair-value pricing, early-close model, assignment probability or tax calculation. Broker collateral rules can differ.

pitfall.title: Cash backing does not protect the share value
pitfall.text: At a $50 strike with 200 shares and $496 net premium, a $45 expiration price still produces a $504 loss. At zero stock value the modeled loss is $9,504.

tools.text: Inspect expiration profit, strike-based cash backing and downside from an entered short put.
Compare a call backed by owned shares using explicit entry cost and trading fees.

name: Profitability index
title: Profitability index: Formula, Example & Limits
description: Profitability index is the present value of a project’s future net cash flows divided by its positive initial investment.
definition: Profitability index is the present value of a project’s future net cash flows divided by its positive initial investment. Under this definition, a value of 1 means discounted future net value equals the initial outlay.
explanation: PI is a ratio; NPV subtracts the outlay from future present value to give a dollar amount. The initial outlay belongs outside the future-flow list. A ratio of discounted positive inflows to all discounted outflows is a different convention.
formula: PI = PV(future net cash flows) / initial outlay = 1 + NPV / initial outlay
formulaNote: One positive initial outlay and manually entered future net flows or a known discounted PV. Periodic flows start at the end of period 1. This is not the alternative ratio of positive inflows to all outflows.

example.title: A $12,000 present value against a $10,000 outlay gives PI of 1.20
example.intro: $10,000 initial investment now; $12,000 present value of future net cash flows, already discounted.
steps: Divide future cash-flow present value by the initial outlay: $12,000 / $10,000.
Subtract the same outlay to reconcile NPV: $12,000 − $10,000 = $2,000. Do not discount the entered present value again.
example.answer: PI is 1.20: $1.20 of modeled future present value per $1 invested. The $2,000 NPV is a separate dollar measure.
example.assumptions: One positive initial outlay and manually entered future net flows or a known discounted PV. Periodic flows start at the end of period 1. This is not the alternative ratio of positive inflows to all outflows.

pitfall.title: A higher ratio need not create more total dollars
pitfall.text: Project size can reverse the PI and NPV rankings. Compare the same timing, discount-rate convention and cash-flow definitions before interpreting either result.

tools.text: Calculate discounted value per dollar of outlay alongside dollar NPV.
Inspect discounted value in dollars with explicit cash-flow timing.

scope: One positive initial outlay and manually entered future net flows or a known discounted PV. Periodic flows start at the end of period 1. This is not the alternative ratio of positive inflows to all outflows.

name: Return on equity
title: Return on equity: Formula, Example & Limits
description: Return on equity compares period net income with representative average book equity for the same ownership scope.
definition: Return on equity compares period net income with representative average book equity for the same ownership scope. It is an accounting earnings-to-equity measure, rather than an investor’s stock-market return.
explanation: The three-factor DuPont identity expresses the same ratio as net margin multiplied by asset turnover and the equity multiplier. Consistent sales, asset and equity definitions let the factors reconcile without changing the underlying earnings.
formula: ROE = net income / average equity; DuPont = margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier
formulaNote: Manual corporate accounting ratios. No financial-statement retrieval, equity valuation or property cash-yield model. Nonpositive equity and equity crossings do not receive a healthy performance score.

example.title: Earn $200,000 on $1.25 million of average equity
example.intro: $200,000 period net income; $1,250,000 representative average book equity for the same ownership scope.
steps: Divide net income by average equity: $200,000 / $1,250,000.
Convert the ratio to a percentage. Use book equity, rather than the market value of the company’s shares.
example.answer: ROE is 16% for the entered period. This is an accounting return, not a shareholder’s market return.
example.assumptions: Manual corporate accounting ratios. No financial-statement retrieval, equity valuation or property cash-yield model. Nonpositive equity and equity crossings do not receive a healthy performance score.

pitfall.title: A smaller equity base can inflate the ratio
pitfall.text: Higher ROE can reflect leverage or a depleted denominator. Zero or negative equity and large within-period balance changes require separate interpretation.

tools.text: Reconcile period earnings, average equity and DuPont factors.
Examine a general gain-to-cost relationship with its own investment and timing assumptions.

name: Substantially equal periodic payments (SEPP)
title: Substantially equal periodic payments (SEPP): Formula, Example & Limits
description: Substantially equal periodic payments are a distribution arrangement that may qualify for an exception to the 10% additional tax on certain early retirement distributions when the applicable requirements are met.
definition: Substantially equal periodic payments are a distribution arrangement that may qualify for an exception to the 10% additional tax on certain early retirement distributions when the applicable requirements are met.
explanation: The modeled first-year methods are the life-expectancy or RMD method, fixed amortization and fixed annuitization. Their payment formulas differ. Calculating one amount does not establish the required ongoing series, account treatment or eligibility.
formula: RMD: balance / expectancy; amortization: balance / level-payment factor; annuitization: balance / mortality annuity factor
formulaNote: First-year estimates for a new single-life traditional IRA series starting from 2023 onward under the rules checked here. No joint lives, inherited accounts, pre-2023 transition, first-year proration, tax eligibility, recapture calculation or installment administration.

example.title: An age-50 RMD-method illustration uses a 36.2-year divisor
example.intro: Birth August 15, 1973; series starts December 1, 2023; entered December 31, 2022 valuation of $400,000; Single Life table.
steps: Age in the illustrated first distribution year is 50. The selected Single Life expectancy is 36.2 years.
Divide the entered account balance by 36.2. This is the RMD calculation method for a SEPP illustration, not a regular age-based required distribution.
The calculator does not establish that the valuation choice or distribution arrangement qualifies for an exception.
example.answer: The illustrated first-year annual amount is $11,049.72. Later-year RMD-method amounts require new inputs and the applicable rules.
example.assumptions: First-year estimates for a new single-life traditional IRA series starting from 2023 onward under the rules checked here. No joint lives, inherited accounts, pre-2023 transition, first-year proration, tax eligibility, recapture calculation or installment administration.

pitfall.title: An additional-tax exception is not tax-free income
pitfall.text: Ordinary income tax can still apply. Treat this dated, single-life first-year illustration as arithmetic; it is not a complete withdrawal plan or a qualification opinion.
